findings: Before repair append/appendSync unconditionally executed ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE and IF; PostgreSQL execution failed at DUPLICATE. claim timeout recovery used TIMESTAMPADD and claim used UPDATE ORDER BY LIMIT; retention used TIMESTAMPADD and DELETE LIMIT.

AuthCenterEventConfig lines 49-97 explicitly constructs Store, publisher and dispatcher for apex.events.outbox.enabled=true or missing. It does not restrict the JDBC database vendor. basic explicitly disables Outbox. Default/prod auth configuration is MySQL, so merely selecting a Spring profile does not select PostgreSQL: JDBC URL/driver, R2DBC URL and Flyway locations must all be overridden for PG. With a PG JDBC DataSource and enabled/default Outbox the SQL path is reachable.

System scans infrastructure; Store is unconditional Repository and dispatcher enabled=true/missing. apex.database.type selects Flyway locations, not the pre-repair Store SQL. Disabling dispatcher is not proof that every append caller disappears.

MySQL DEAD duplicate resurrection also had a confirmed defect: status was assigned before attempts/next_attempt_at/locks/error, so subsequent IF(status='DEAD') tested the changed status. Assignment ordering now implements the existing documented revival contract.

No Outbox dialect option existed in Store. Repair selects PostgreSQL using the actual Connection DatabaseMetaData product name, preserving the existing constructor and transaction connection. PG uses ON CONFLICT, bounded locked subquery with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, interval arithmetic and bounded delete subquery. Other existing vendor behavior remains MySQL SQL. State updates and token predicates remain unchanged.

Not exercised or repaired here, and not claimed PG compatible. It is separate from the P0 candidate sys_domain_event_outbox path.

runtime.mysql_concurrency_limit: Existing default MySQL isolation may deadlock with SQLState 40001 during overlapping claims. Observed on first green attempt. Final test permits one retry only for that SQLState, representing the scheduler next poll; no production retry or isolation behavior was changed. This does not establish deadlock-free claims.
runtime.time_limit: Container database time differed from host time; test expiry fixtures derive from SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Production retry time still uses Instant.now as before; clock/timezone configuration correctness was not repaired or established.
